headline: Congress passed a resolution on May 21, 2018, to cancel a 2017 Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rule on fair lending for car loans arranged through dealers.
what_it_does: This resolution uses the Congressional Review Act to overturn a rule from the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau about indirect auto lending. Indirect auto lending is when a car dealer arranges a loan from a third-party lender. The rule gave guidance on following the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, which bars lenders from discriminating in credit decisions. With this resolution, the rule no longer applies.

who_it_affects.group: Third-party auto lenders that buy car loans from dealers
who_it_affects.how: They no longer have to follow the Bureau's 2017 guidance on fair lending compliance for indirect auto loans.

who_it_affects.group: Car dealers that arrange financing for buyers
who_it_affects.how: They are no longer subject to the Bureau's 2017 guidance when they arrange loans for customers through outside lenders.

who_it_affects.group: People who finance a car through a dealer
who_it_affects.how: The rule that would have set fair lending guidance for their loans is no longer in effect.

when_it_takes_effect: The resolution was enacted on May 21, 2018, and took effect that day.
